H1.title: The shipped visibility gate has no committed regression
H1.resolution: Committed the negative control: test_hide_window plan knob (smoke-mode-only) builds the window ordered-out, fixture sidecar now answers the MCP smoke so the cycle reaches the window step, and tests/test_desktop_child.py::test_fault_hidden_window_fails_the_cycle asserts exit 1 + lifecycle-failed 'window not visible after navigate' + orphan-shutdown + NO window-ready; paired pass arm pins the payload. Demonstrated: gate reverted -> FAILED (assert 0 == 1, window-ready emitted on an ordered-out window); gate restored -> 2 passed.

M1.title: `{"visible": true}` claims more than `NSWindow.isVisible` measures
M1.anchor: /// Ok additionally attests the native window is observably visi
M1.resolution: Renamed the event field {visible:true} -> {window_ordered_in:true} and rewrote navigate_window's doc comment to state the AppKit semantics exactly (NSWindow.isVisible via tao; true for an occluded/off-screen/zero-sized/other-Space window; no WebView render state), plus a README subsection recording what window-ready does and does not attest. The gate itself is unchanged; only the claim was narrowed. Err reason strings left alone - they are honest in the negative direction.

M2.title: Absence is concluded with no live proof the probe still works
M2.resolution: The 15s poll now binds the suppressed RuntimeError as last_probe_error instead of discarding it, and absence is no longer claimable on a stale liveness claim: on timeout the control pid is RE-PROBED, and a control that now raises or reads 0 fails the test naming the PROBE rather than the supervisor. Both blind-probe causes (headless vs denied Accessibility) are named in the sweep skip message.

M3.title: Module docstring contradicts the test the file just gained
M3.anchor: precedent, they carry NO secondary skip guard:
M3.resolution: Module docstring now records the single named exception to the no-secondary-skip-guard convention and why it is sound (a probe that may conclude ABSENCE must be positive-controllable, so it skips rather than asserting into the dark), and notes the conftest zero-skip gate converts that skip into a session failure.

M4.title: `make desktop-conformance` can no longer pass on Linux
M4.resolution: Recorded rather than papered over: apps/desktop/README.md gains a 'make desktop-conformance is macOS-only today' subsection beside the existing m6 non-claims, naming both skipping tests (the native-window regression and test_desktop_contract.py's pre-existing win32 skipif), stating the gate is red off macOS with no way to make it green, why weakening the zero-skip rule was rejected, and what a future milestone owes. The module docstring cross-references it.

L1.title: Positive control races across two osascript invocations
L1.resolution: Cheap and adjacent to the M2 edit in the same test: the sweep + re-count now retries up to 3 times before failing, so a swept process closing its last window between the two osascript round trips re-sweeps instead of reddening the run.
